videos.script: A course cover is one line of SwiftUI. AsyncImage, a URL, and a placeholder. {{line}} That line makes three decisions for you. How big the picture is in memory. Whether it is kept. And what happens when its row scrolls away. {{sums}} Today you measure the first one. A photograph from a phone's camera, forty kilobytes on the network. Decoded, forty-six megabytes. {{thumb}} And the square it is drawn in needs two hundred times less. {{down}} So the fix is not a smaller download. It is a smaller decode, and ImageIO does that on a Mac. {{cache}} Then a cache the app controls. Ten rows ask for three covers at the same moment, and three downloads happen. {{evict}} And you watch one full-size photograph push everything else out of it. {{list}} Last, the list itself. One cache for every row, small pictures decoded off the main thread, and rows that stop waiting when they leave.
